transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well... occupational health sent me. They, um, they say my weight is dangerously low for someone who runs presses and does fabrication all day. I don't really see it like that. I honestly just thought I was getting leaner. You know, more disciplined. But... yeah. That's why they told me to come.
Are you afraid of gaining weight?
...Yeah, I guess. It's just... if the scale goes up even a little bit, I kind of panic. I feel like I'm going to lose all the control I've worked for. I just don't want to end up heavy again.
Do you ever eat a large amount of food in a short period of time?
No. I don't do that.
Do you ever make yourself vomit after eating?
No... I've never done that.
Do you often limit the types or amounts of food you eat?

...I suppose. I just stick to a routine. Usually it's just black coffee before the early shift... maybe half a protein bar at lunch. And then just a small bowl of vegetables after yoga. It's just... if I eat more than that, the whole day just feels out of control. So I keep it to that.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight recently?

I don't know about significant. Occupational health at work is actually who sent me here. They keep saying my weight is... dangerously low for someone running presses and doing fabrication all day. But... I don't really see it that way. I honestly just thought I was getting leaner. Just... more disciplined.
Do you ever feel like you've lost control while eating?
...No. I don't really let that happen. Like I said, I'm pretty disciplined about it. I just stick to my routine.
Do you think you would still restrict your food intake if you weren't worried about gaining weight?
...I don't know. I haven't really thought about it like that. It's just... it's just what I do.
Would you say your goal is to be thinner, or is it more about not being heavier than you are now?

I guess... it's about not being heavier. I just... if I step on the scale and the number goes up, even just a fraction of a pound, I... I get really anxious. It feels like if it goes up, I'm going to lose all this control I've built up, and... and I'll just end up heavy again. I can't let that happen.
Do you think you would be happy with your current weight if you didn't have to worry about gaining more?
I don't know. I can't really... imagine not worrying about it. So I'm not sure.
Do you think you would still want to lose more weight if you weren't afraid of gaining weight?
I... I really couldn't say. It's hard to separate the two. I just... I don't know.
Is your main goal with eating and exercising to achieve a certain body shape or size, or is it more about avoiding a specific weight or size you don't want to be?
I'm... not really sure. I just... I try to stay where I am. I don't really think about it like that.
Do you think your eating habits would change if you felt secure that you wouldn't gain weight?
I... probably not. It's just... my routine at this point. I don't really spend time thinking about "what ifs" like that.
Do you think you would still try to lose weight even if you felt completely safe from gaining weight in the future?
I don't know. I... I can't really picture that. I just do what I do.
Is your goal of restricting your food intake more about achieving a certain ideal weight or body shape, or is it solely about preventing weight gain?

I don't really have an ideal weight, I guess. It's... it's just about the scale. If it goes up, even just a little bit, I... I panic. I just feel like I'm going to lose all the control I've worked for. I just... I can't end up heavy again. So I just have to keep it from going up.
Do you think you would be content with your body shape and size if you were at a healthy weight?

I... I don't know about content. Even now, when I catch my reflection in the shop window at work, or... or in the bathroom mirror, it's just... I can't. All I see is my stomach and my thighs. They just look too big. It just ruins the rest of my day, honestly. So... I can't imagine being okay with being bigger.
Is your fear of gaining weight the main reason you restrict what you eat?

I guess. It's mostly about... keeping things in order. Most days I just stick to coffee before the early shift. Then maybe half a protein bar at lunch. And... a small bowl of vegetables after yoga. I just... if I eat more than that, the whole day just feels out of control. I can't handle that.
Is your fear of gaining weight the only reason you limit your food intake?
I... I don't really know. I guess so. Like I said, it's just... about keeping things in order. I don't really sit around analyzing it. I just know I can't let the scale go up.
Is your fear of gaining weight the reason you eat so little?

I mean... yeah. I just said that. It's just... if I see the number on the scale go up, even just a fraction of a pound, I just... I panic. I feel like I'm going to lose all the control I've worked so hard for, and... and just end up heavy again. I can't let that happen.
Would you say you restrict your food intake more because you want to lose weight or because you want to prevent yourself from gaining weight?

I... I feel like I just answered this. It's about not gaining. 

I just want to maintain the control I have. Like I said, if that number creeps up even a little bit, I panic. I just can't let myself go back to being heavy. That's really all it is.
